title: Mechanical Engineering Fundamentals

canonicalTerminology.definition: A free-body diagram isolates a body and represents the external forces and moments acting on it for engineering analysis.

claims.text: Mechanical analysis of railway components commonly uses equilibrium, motion, energy, stress and power relationships while respecting real boundary conditions and uncertainties.
claims.applicabilityNote: Level-neutral educational statement; adapt depth without changing the canonical fact.

equations.limitation: Classical rigid-body teaching relationship; model validity depends on the chosen system boundary and assumptions.

visualSpecs.purpose: Teach force and moment representation on a simplified railway component.

prohibitedUnsupportedClaims: Do not convert simplified teaching loads into component acceptance limits.
Do not treat analytical examples as validated design calculations.
